findings.description: packages/gen-eval/src/gen_eval/__main__.py:324 — the runtime CLI still loads every descriptor with `InterfaceDescriptor.from_yaml()`. Generated service descriptors write the operation model at `operations` (scripts/generate_service_descriptor.py:122), but the base model ignores that top-level field, so `build_operation_coverage()` sees no `operations` and falls back to one flat operation per element. A generated descriptor where `acquire_lock` is exposed as HTTP+MCP+CLI and a scenario exercises `POST /locks/acquire` will report element-level operations like `mcp:acquire_lock` / `cli:lock acquire` as uncovered instead of reporting operation `acquire_lock` as covered per D4.

openspec/changes/derive-descriptors-from-contracts/tasks.md:319 — task 5.3 promises that migrating `evaluation/descriptor.yaml` to a derived tool descriptor makes dogfood report the contracted flag count, but the generated tool descriptor stores flag units in top-level `commands` (scripts/generate_tool_descriptor.py:163) while the runtime loader at `__main__.py:324` constructs only `InterfaceDescriptor`. That base `all_interfaces()` only reads `services[*].commands` (descriptor.py:285), so the migrated descriptor will still have zero declared interfaces unless Phase 5 also adds archetype-aware descriptor loading.

packages/gen-eval/src/gen_eval/service_descriptor.py:311 — OpenAPI path-item parameters are not merged into each operation before MCP projection, and `$ref` path items are skipped by the `for method, raw in item.items()` loop. For a standard contract like `/items/{id}: parameters: [{name: id, in: path, required: true}]` with `get.operationId: get_item`, `_flatten_parameters()` only sees `raw.get('parameters')`, so the derived MCP input schema omits the required `id`. The same omission happens for referenced path items, where the operation is never extracted at all.

packages/gen-eval/src/gen_eval/evaluator.py:580 — `_cli_identifiers()` scans all tokens for flags and never stops at the conventional `--` option terminator. A CLI step with `args: ['--mode','template-only','--','--descriptor']` and declared units `{'cli:--mode','cli:--descriptor'}` records both flags, even though the second token is a literal positional value after `--`; coverage is falsely credited for `cli:--descriptor`.

packages/gen-eval/src/gen_eval/verify/surfaces.py:65 — `verify_argparse()` only iterates the root parser's `_actions` and does not descend into `_SubParsersAction` choices. For a parser with subcommand `lock` whose subparser declares undocumented `--force`, calling `verify_argparse(root_parser, descriptor)` returns no violation because the subparser action has no option strings; the exposed element `cli:lock --force` is hidden from the subset verifier.

packages/gen-eval/src/gen_eval/service_descriptor.py:229 — `operations_for_element()` compares every surface as `f'{surface}:{element}'`, but HTTP identifiers are deliberately unprefixed. Calling `operations_for_element('http', 'GET /locks/active')` on the fixture returns `[]` even though `list_active_locks` is served by that HTTP element; only MCP/CLI callers using unprefixed element names can succeed.
